dataSource.fetchedBy: research agent, verified against the official source
dataSource.notes:
SOURCE. Jersey Mike's official nutrition page (jerseymikes.com/menu/nutrition) is a JS-only calculator that renders nothing in static HTML. I traced its Nuxt bundle to the first-party data API that backs it: GET https://subs.jerseymikes.com/nutrition/{productId}/{sizeId} (endpoint constants NUTRITION="/nutrition/data" and PRODUCT_NUTRITION_DATA="/nutrition" in chunk BTlHHIuq.js; baseURL = runtime config subsURLBase = https://subs.jerseymikes.com/). Every number below is a raw field from that API — no aggregator, no estimation. I pulled all 50 sub products at size_id=2 plus the sides products.

SIZE BASIS. Everything is authored at size_id=2, which Jersey Mike's labels "Regular" (their sizes are Mini / Regular / Giant, confirmed on their FAQ). Caution on the brief's "7-inch": the official source never states an inch measurement for any size, so I did not put "7-inch" in any serving description. It is the Regular size, full stop.

WHY PORTIONS ARE RECIPE-SPECIFIC (the one real modeling decision). The API returns nutrition per ingredient *per parent sub*, and portions genuinely differ by recipe — Turkey is 111.2 cal on #7 Turkey and Provolone but only 55.6 cal as one layer of the #8 Club Sub; Ham ranges 56.2–110.8 across five subs. There is no single published "one serving of turkey" figure. So each protein is authored at the portion from the sub where that meat is the star, and the serving description names that sub explicitly. Cheeses and toppings use the dominant standard value (e.g. Lettuce 11.9 cal on all 24 cold subs vs 7.9 on hot subs; cold-sub value used). Breads are identical across all 50 products, so they carry no ambiguity.

VALUES ARE NOT REVERSE-ENGINEERED. These are line items as published, not back-solved from combo totals. Calories are rounded to whole numbers and macros to 1 decimal from the source's 6-decimal values.

DEFAULTS = "MIKE'S WAY". The calculator marks ingredients with inclusion_type "D" as pre-selected. For cold subs those are exactly onions, lettuce, tomatoes, olive oil blend, red wine vinegar, oregano and salt — which matches Jersey Mike's own published definition of Mike's Way. So the presets below are each sub as served Mike's Way.

HOW THE PRESET TOTALS WERE DERIVED. The site has no separate published sub-level total; its own footer sums the selected ingredient rows, applying FDA rounding to the calorie total only (helper: <5 → 0, ≤50 → nearest 5, >50 → nearest 10) and leaving protein raw. I reproduced that exact function, so publishedCalories/publishedProtein are the figures the official calculator displays for that sub in its default state. I only included a sub as a preset if every one of its default ingredients matches the canonical portion in my menu — that is why the 12 presets are all single-meat subs. Summing my components reproduces each published total within ±4 cal and ±0.1 g protein; that residual is only integer-rounding against the site's round-to-nearest-10, not a data disagreement.

SAUCE CAVEAT. "Ranch" exists as two distinct ingredient ids at different portions (187.9 cal on #26 Bacon Ranch Chicken Cheese Steak, 205.3 cal on Grilled Turkey Bacon Ranch). I shipped the #26 portion. Olive Oil Blend (250 cal) and Mayo (261 cal) look large but are the source's actual full-sub pours — they are the single biggest lever on a Jersey Mike's sub and are correct as published.
